This report is specific to one comparison: the effect of UK vs. mock in self-renewing samples. It begins post-filtering with the same dataset used in the previous report, then subsetted out just the 4/30 SR samples to do the statistics.

The statistical contrast was set up as UK / mock, so positive log2FC indicates higher binding in UK. 

**Significance table excel download:**

```{r download_report, echo = FALSE}
xfun::embed_file(
path = "../plots_and_tables/drug_effect_in_SR_significance_tables_and_annotations.xlsx",
text = "Download statistics")

```


## Differential Binding testing

With a cutoff for significance of FDR < 0.05 and abs(log2FC) > 1,
there were this many differentially bound peaks:

| caller | lower in UK (logFC < 0) | higher in UK (logFC > 0) |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| macs3 | 148 | 29 |
| genrich | 99 | 15 |


### Volcano plots

The way the statistics were setup, a positive logFC indicates higher binding (more reads) in
the UK-treated SR cells. I show volcano plots two ways: focusing just on the genes, and then with color-coding based upon the location of the peak relative to the nearest gene.

### bar plots of annotations

The following graphs show how the significant peaks were annotated, relative to the
nearest gene. There are two bars per annotation category, which reflect the count of
peaks with logFC greater than or less than zero, meaning whether the differential binding
indicated higher binding in UK or mock. 

#### macs3 

![](../plots_and_tables/barchart_drug_effect_in_SR_annotations_macs3.png)

#### genrich

![](../plots_and_tables/barchart_drug_effect_in_SR_annotations_genrich.png)
### CPM plots

For the top 20 significant peaks with higher, and lower, binding, I plot
the CPM (counts-per-million). Note that since there were < 20 peaks with higher binding in UK, there are fewer than 40 panels total. 

I have labeled each significant peak by its peak name, nearest gene, and annotation.

#### macs3

![](../plots_and_tables/cpm_plots_drug_effect_in_SR_top_DEGs_macs3.png)

#### genrich

![](../plots_and_tables/cpm_plots_drug_effect_in_SR_top_DEGs_genrich.png)

### differential binding heatmaps

The last per-caller plots for the differential binding statistics are heatmaps
of the CPM for all genes. This is very similar to the CPM plots above, except
rather than showing log10(CPM), the log10(CPM) have been z-scaled to emphasize
relative differences. 

#### macs3

![](../plots_and_tables/heatmap_drug_effect_in_SR_DEGs_macs3.png)


#### genrich

![](../plots_and_tables/heatmap_drug_effect_in_SR_DEGs_genrich.png)

### Quick caller comparison

The following scatterplot show the log2FC for each caller, for only the genes which
had significantly differential binding in either caller. I averaged the log2FC and FDR
when multiple peaks were annotated to a single gene. 

I think color-coded by which caller the gene was significant within. Note that many 
genes had peaks with differential binding in both callers, and even when only one caller
was significant, usually the log2FC was in the same direction in the other caller.

![](../plots_and_tables/scatterplot__drug_effect_in_SR_sig_genes.png)
